items.prompt: Intake is done, all three verifications PASSED, the decision is APPROVED, and one closing condition is FAILED. Which stage does reconcileWorkflow return?
items.answer: CONDITIONS, with a reason naming the failed condition
distractors: APPROVED, as the decision outranks any later conditions
CREDIT_DECISIONING, as a failure reopens the decision
VERIFICATION, as any FAILED status sends it back there
items.explanation: Rules run in order: decline, servicing, disbursement, intake, verification, decisioning (only PENDING or REFER), then the failed-condition rule, which returns CONDITIONS before the APPROVED rule is reached. The VERIFICATION rule looks at verifications, not conditions.

items.prompt: An APPROVED application with no conditions receives a newer EMPLOYMENT_CHECK event with status FAILED. What stage does it move to?
items.answer: VERIFICATION, because verification rules come before decisions
distractors: APPROVED, because a recorded approval cannot be undone by a check
CONDITIONS, because a failure after approval becomes a condition
DENIED, because a failed required check declines the application
items.explanation: The verification rule fires when any verification is FAILED or a required one is not PASSED, and it comes before every decision-based rule, so the approval no longer holds the stage.

items.prompt: A loan has been disbursed (disbursedAt is set). An underwriter then records a DECLINED decision. What stage does the application end in?
items.answer: DENIED, since the decline rule is checked first
distractors: DISBURSEMENT, since funding outranks a decline
400, since decisions are closed after funding
SERVICING_HANDOFF, since the funds already left
items.explanation: recordDecision only refuses when the derived stage is VERIFICATION. The reconciler tests decisionOutcome DECLINED / deniedAt before servicingHandedOffAt and disbursedAt, so a funded loan becomes DENIED.

items.prompt: CREDIT_PULL is PASSED at providerSequence 5. An event with providerSequence 3 and status FAILED arrives. What happens to the verification?
items.answer: It stays PASSED; the event is kept but marked out of order
distractors: It becomes FAILED, as the latest event to arrive is the one applied
The event is refused with 409 and is not stored in any table
It stays PASSED, and the stale event is dropped without a row
items.explanation: shouldApply is input >= current (3 >= 5 is false), so the verification is not updated. The event row is still created with appliedToWorkflow false and receivedOutOfOrder true.

items.prompt: CREDIT_PULL is PASSED at providerSequence 5. A second event also carrying providerSequence 5 arrives with status FAILED. What happens?
items.answer: It is applied, and the verification becomes FAILED
distractors: It is ignored, as sequence 5 was already seen
It is stored as out of order and not applied
It is refused as a duplicate by a unique index
items.explanation: The guard is >=, so an equal sequence counts as fresh: the event is applied and overwrites PASSED with FAILED. isOutOfOrder uses <, so it is not flagged either.

items.prompt: A LOAN_OFFICER calls POST /api/applications/:id/submit for an INTAKE application. The service would allow loan officers. What is the response?
items.answer: 403 from the wrapper, as only BORROWER has application:submit
distractors: 200, as submitApplication lets both borrowers and loan officers in
403 from the service, as it only lets the creator submit the file
400, as loan officers must also send a confirmReady flag of false
items.explanation: The route declares permission application:submit and createRouteHandler asserts it before the handler runs; in the matrix only BORROWER has it. The service's own role check (borrower or loan officer) is never reached.

items.prompt: An underwriter records APPROVED while DOCUMENT_CHECK is still PENDING. What does recordDecision do?
items.answer: 400: verification checks must pass before decisioning
distractors: 200: the approval is saved and the stage stays put
409: the decision conflicts with an open verification
403: underwriters may not decide unverified files
items.explanation: recordDecision derives the stage first; when it is VERIFICATION it throws badRequest("All required verification checks must pass before decisioning.") before opening the transaction.

items.prompt: After a write, the derived stage equals the stored stage but the derived reason text differs from stageReason. What does reconcileAndPersistStage do?
items.answer: It updates the row and writes a transition with equal from/to stages
distractors: Nothing, as a transition is written only when the stage itself changes
It updates the reason alone and writes no ApplicationTransition row
It throws, since a transition must have a different from and to stage
items.explanation: The condition is nextStage !== stage OR reason !== stageReason. A reason-only change still bumps stateVersion and creates a transition whose fromStage equals toStage.

items.prompt: A SERVICING_AGENT requests the detail of an application that is in the CONDITIONS stage. What is the response?
items.answer: 404, as servicing agents see only funded files
distractors: 200, as the detail read route needs no permission
403, as servicing agents lack view-pipeline here
200 with borrower income and contact data hidden
items.explanation: For SERVICING_AGENT the visibility filter is stage in [DISBURSEMENT, SERVICING_HANDOFF]; the lookup finds nothing and ensureReadableApplication or the query service throws notFound.

items.prompt: Borrower A creates an application and sets coApplicant.userId to borrower B's user id. What can borrower B now do?
items.answer: See the application, as B is now linked as a party
distractors: Nothing, as only the creator can read a borrower file
See it only after a loan officer approves the link
Nothing, as party userIds are checked against the caller
items.explanation: Borrower visibility is parties.some({ userId: session.user.id }), and the create schema accepts any userId on each party. Ids are listed by GET /api/session.

items.prompt: A borrower creates an application with requestedAmount 1000000000000 (one trillion). The column is Decimal(12,2). What comes back?
items.answer: 500 Internal server error, from the database overflow
distractors: 400 Validation failed, as the amount is out of range
201, with the amount silently capped to fit the column
201, with the amount stored as a rounded float value
items.explanation: The zod schema only requires positive(); the value passes validation and overflows numeric(12,2) at insert. That Prisma error is neither a ZodError nor an AppError, so errorResponse returns 500.

items.prompt: A loan officer posts a fresh (applied) provider event that changes the stage. How is the resulting ApplicationTransition attributed?
items.answer: To the system, with triggeredBySystem true and no user id
distractors: To the loan officer, as the user who posted the event
To the provider, with its providerReference as actor
To nobody, as provider events never write a transition
items.explanation: ingestExternalVerificationEvent passes actorUserId null when shouldApply is true, and createTransition sets triggeredBySystem to actorUserId === null. A stale event is attributed to the user instead; the audit log always names the user.

items.back: 1 declined or deniedAt: DENIED; 2 servicingHandedOffAt: SERVICING_HANDOFF; 3 disbursedAt: DISBURSEMENT; 4 no intake: INTAKE; 5 any FAILED or missing/non-PASSED required verification: VERIFICATION; 6 decision PENDING or REFER: CREDIT_DECISIONING; 7 a FAILED condition: CONDITIONS; 8 an OPEN condition: CONDITIONS; 9 APPROVED: APPROVED; else unchanged. The order is the policy.

items.front: How does the provider-event sequence guard work, and where does it fall short?
items.back: Each verification keeps a providerSequence high-water mark. An event below it is stored with appliedToWorkflow false and receivedOutOfOrder true; an equal or higher one overwrites the verification. Gaps: equal sequences re-apply, there is no row lock, no idempotency key, and the "provider" is a logged-in loan officer.

items.front: In what order does createRouteHandler process a request?
items.back: Resolve the session; 401 if none and the route is not allowAnonymous; assert the declared permission (403); run the handler; in the catch, ZodError becomes 400, AppError keeps its status, anything else is logged and returned as 500.

items.front: Why is it a problem that recordDecision and disburseApplication run their guards before prisma.$transaction?
items.back: The guard reads state outside the transaction, so a concurrent write can change the facts between the check and the update. The transaction makes the writes atomic, but not the decision to allow them; there is no optimistic locking on stateVersion.
